suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a note about prefix caching TTFT measurement methodology: when measuring prefix caching benefit, ensure the server is already warmed up before running the comparison test. The first request after server start with graph mode includes ~100s of graph capture warmup time, which conflates cold-start overhead with actual caching measurement. Recommended approach: send 1-2 warm-up requests first, then run the before/after prefix caching comparison.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: prefix-caching-and-config-tuning: first request TTFT was 15622ms (includes graph warmup), second was 137ms. The ratio (0.009) far exceeded the 0.80 threshold but is not a true measurement of prefix caching benefit in steady state. The metric passed VAL-GRAPH-005 but the methodology is misleading.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Consider adding a 'start-config-tuned' command entry to services.yaml pointing to /root/benchmark-scripts/launch-config-tuned.sh, so workers can discover and use the optimized startup script without needing to know its path. Currently this script is only discoverable via library documentation.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Both optimization-worker features created launch scripts (/root/benchmark-scripts/launch-graphs.sh, launch-config-tuned.sh) but neither is registered in services.yaml. Workers in future milestones needing to start vLLM with the best config must read library docs to find it.
